issues.failure_explanation: The displayed decomposition diag(B^TB,1)+[0 γB^Ty; γy^TB γ²‖x+y‖²] is not [B,(x+y)γ]ᵀ[B,(x+y)γ]: its (n+1,n+1) entry is 1+γ²‖x+y‖² instead of γ²‖x+y‖² (it exceeds the true Gram matrix by e_{n+1}e_{n+1}ᵀ). Weyl's inequality applied to this wrong matrix lower-bounds λ_min of a larger matrix, which does not lower-bound σ_min([B,b])²; the subsequent replacements λ_max diag(BᵀB,1)→σ_max²(B) and λ_min diag(BᵀB,1)→σ_min²(B) additionally require σ_min(B)≤1≤σ_max(B), which is never assumed. The claimed bound is false: for B=[1;0], x=0, y=[1;1], γ=1 (all hypotheses hold) κ([B,b])=(3+√5)/2≈2.618, while the bound gives √(3+2√2)=1+√2≈2.414; equivalently the proof's step σ_min²([B,b])≥2−√2≈0.586 fails since actually σ_min²([B,b])=(3−√5)/2≈0.382.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rebuild from the correct split diag(BᵀB,γ²‖x+y‖²)+[0 γBᵀy; γyᵀB 0]: Weyl gives κ([B,b]) ≤ √([max(σ_max²(B),γ²‖x+y‖²)+γ‖Bᵀy‖₂]/[min(σ_min²(B),γ²‖x+y‖²)−γ‖Bᵀy‖₂]), a weaker bound that can be vacuous; the advertised closed form is abandoned.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised no-assumption bound on κ([B,b]) is false, and item 2 (it:thm:cool-2), which substitutes γ=1/‖x+y‖ into item 1, inherits the false bound; the main result of Section 2 collapses.
issues.title: thm:cool: incorrect Gram-matrix decomposition yields a false condition-number bound
issues.why_classification: The central bound is false as stated (explicit counterexample) and the proof's key decomposition is wrong; the only supported repair produces a different, weaker, often vacuous bound, so the substantive result is abandoned.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs √(1+4t²)≤ε with t=‖Bᵀy‖₂/‖x+y‖₂, i.e. t≤√(ε²−1)/2, but the stated hypothesis only gives t≤(ε²−1)/4, which is strictly weaker once ε>√5 (e.g. ε=3, t=2: √(1+16)≈4.12>3). So the substitution 1±√(1+4t²)→1±ε is unjustified. The statement also silently requires ε>1 for the hypothesis to be non-vacuous, ‖x+y‖₂>0 for the normalization, and 2σ_min²(B)+1−ε>0 for the final denominator; for ε≤1 the conclusion can fail even when Bᵀy=0 (the bound κ(B)√(1+f) can drop below κ(B) while κ([B,(x+y)/‖x+y‖])=κ(B)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to ‖Bᵀy‖₂²/‖x+y‖₂²≤(ε²−1)/4 (equivalently ‖Bᵀy‖₂/‖x+y‖₂≤√(ε²−1)/2) and add ε>1, ‖x+y‖₂>0, 2σ_min²(B)+1−ε>0; the form κ(B)√(1+f(B,ε)) then follows.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the κ(B)√(1+f(B,ε)) bound in item 2 rests on an inference the stated hypothesis does not support; as stated the item is unproved (and, via item 1, false).
issues.title: thm:cool item 2: hypothesis does not imply the key epsilon-substitution
issues.why_classification: A contained change to the hypothesis (plus side conditions) restores the proof and the conclusion's form survives, but the admissible class of y and the conditions on ε change, so the repair is more than a typo yet leaves a comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \( Q \) be an orthonormal \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \)

issues.failure_explanation: The formula uses (m−n)/2 degrees of freedom, i.e. dim span(B)=n. If B is rank deficient, dim span(B)⊥ = m−rank(B) > m−n and the law of ‖P_B⊥(Y)‖ changes; e.g. B=0 gives ‖P_B⊥(Y)‖=‖Y‖ with a χ²_m law, not χ²_{m−n}. The corollary drops the full-column-rank hypothesis that the invoked projection theorem carries.

failure_location.quote:
Let \( B \) be an \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \), and \( Y \in \mathbb{R}^m \) be a random vector with i.i.d. components \( Y_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2) \). Then:
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(\|P_{B}^{\perp}(Y)\\|_2 \leq \varepsilon) = 1 - \mathcal{Q}^{ma}_{(m-n)/2}(0, \frac{\varepsilon}{\sigma}).
    \]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'B has full column rank' to the statement; the formula then holds as written.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary is false as stated for rank-deficient B; downstream uses (thm:noise-ls) apply it only to full-rank/orthonormal matrices, so they are unaffected.
issues.title: cor:golden3: false for rank-deficient B (missing full-rank hypothesis)
issues.why_classification: A single standard hypothesis restores the statement with no change to the conclusion or to any downstream use.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The probability that the norm of \( X + P_{Q}^{\perp}(Y) \) exceeds \( \varepsilon \) is given by \( \mathcal{Q}^{ma}_{(m-n)/2}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2}{\sigma},\frac{\varepsilon}{\sigma}\right) \)

issues.failure_explanation: The probability Q^{(ma)}_{(m-n)/2}(‖X‖/σ, ε/σ) is increasing in ‖X‖, so under the theorem's assumptions (X arbitrary in span(Q⊥)) the worst case is X=0, where it equals Q^{(ma)}_{(m-n)/2}(0,25.6)=Γ((m−n)/2,655.36)/Γ((m−n)/2)=P(χ²_{m−n}>655.36)≈0 for m−n≥100 — not ≥0.9734. The corollary omits any lower bound on ‖X‖ (e.g. ‖X‖₂=1, the setting of the paper's numerical tests, which gives probability ≈1).

failure_location.quote:
with \( m-n \geq 100 \), \( \sigma = 2^{-8} \), and \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{10} \), we have:
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(\|X + P_{Q}^{\perp}(Y)\\|_2 > 1/10) \geq 0.9734.
    \]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis such as ‖X‖₂=1 (or a computed lower threshold) and verify the constant against the Marcum-Q value; without a norm condition on X no version with the same constant can hold.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's numerical guarantee is false as stated; it is standalone (not used downstream), so the damage is confined to this illustrative claim.
issues.title: cor:added-1: numerical probability bound fails for small ‖X‖
issues.why_classification: A false universal numerical claim; the repair adds a new premise on ‖X‖ and re-establishes the constant — a limited weakening that leaves a comparable illustrative result but withdraws the advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The noncentral F statistic is the ratio of squared norms, (Z₂²/(m−n))/(Z₁²/n), not (Z₂/(m−n))/(Z₁/n). Hence the event {Z₂/Z₁<ε₂/ε₁} equals {F′<nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²)} and the displayed probability is the survival function 1−F′_{m−n,n}(nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²);‖X‖²/σ²), not F′_{m−n,n}(nε₂/((m−n)ε₁);‖X‖²/σ²) as stated (unsquared argument, and CDF in place of the survival probability). The statement is incorrect as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side by the survival function 1−F′_{m−n,n}(nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²);‖X‖₂²/σ²) (or define F′ as the survival function with the squared argument); the noncentral-F form of the theorem survives and both dependent corollaries are repaired by the same substitution.
issues.overall_effect: The exact probability in thm:noise-ls is wrong; cor:main and cor:added-2 inherit the unsquared F argument in their 'with probability at least' guarantees.
issues.title: thm:noise-ls: wrong statistic and argument in the noncentral F probability
issues.why_classification: A contained correction (square the epsilons; use the survival function) restores the theorem and its two dependents without changing the result's nature or the downstream architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Dividing the two displayed singular-value bounds yields κ([B,cγ])≤max{σ_max(B),γ}/min{σ_min(B),γ}·κ([Q,c]) = max{κ(B),‖B‖₂/γ,γ‖B†‖₂}κ([Q,c]) — the second line. The first line replaces κ([Q,c]) by κ([Q,cγ]) and drops the γ-scaling of the coefficient; the asserted equality between the two forms is false in general (e.g. γ=2, ‖B‖₂=3, σ_min(B)=1.5 gives coefficients 3 vs 2), and κ([Q,cγ])≥κ([Q,c]) also fails in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the spurious first line; the correct consequence of items 1–2 is the second line directly.
issues.overall_effect: Only the intermediate display line is wrong; the item's final bound (the second line) is correct and is what lm:cond-ls uses, so no downstream result is affected.
issues.title: thm:min-max-cond item 3: false intermediate equality in the displayed bound
issues.why_classification: The theorem's actual conclusions are correct and correctly proved; removing one erroneous intermediate display line is a local fix with no mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Liesen's formula (thm:strak, eq:miro) expects the unscaled residual ‖r‖=min_u‖c−Qu‖, but lm:cond-ls defines ‖r‖=min_z‖cγ−Bz‖=γ·(unscaled residual), so the substitution introduces spurious γ-factors. The bound is false for general γ: with B=[1;0], c=[1;1], γ=2 (columns of B have norm 1) κ([B,cγ])=(9+√65)/4≈4.27 while the stated bound gives κ(B)(9+√17)/8≈1.64. The proof's step max{σ_max(B),1}/min{σ_min(B),1}=κ(B) is only the γ=1 case of thm:min-max-cond item 3; for general γ one needs σ_min(B)≤γ≤σ_max(B), which is not assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with γ absorbed into c (WLOG γ=1): for B with columns of norm 1, κ([B,c])≤κ(B)((1+‖c‖²)+√((1+‖c‖²)²−4‖r‖²))/(2‖r‖) with ‖r‖=min_z‖c−Bz‖; the general-γ statement is then recovered by c′=cγ with no spurious factors.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is false as stated for γ outside [σ_min(B),σ_max(B)]; the γ=1 case used by cor:cond-ls remains valid, so cor:cond-ls is unaffected.
issues.title: lm:cond-ls: bound false for general gamma (scaled residual fed into Liesen's formula)
issues.why_classification: The statement is false and its quantitative bound must be corrected, but the repair is a restatement recognizing that γ is redundant — the substantive claim (κ(B) times the Liesen factor of the residual) survives, so the loss is limited to the erroneous formulation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \) with columns of norm 1, \( q\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), such that \( \|q\|_2=1 \).

issues.failure_explanation: The vector q appears in the conclusion without being introduced or defined anywhere in the statement; the invoked cor:cond-ls additionally requires B to have columns of norm 1 and q to be a unit vector, neither of which cor:main assumes. The intended q is the normalized noisy column (X+Y)/‖X+Y‖ (as in cor:added-2), whose residual equals thm:noise-ls's r, but as written the corollary is ill-posed.

failure_location.quote: Assume \( B \) is an \( m \times n \) full rank matrix \( (m > n) \) and \( X\in \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp}) \subset \mathbb{R}^m= \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp})\bigoplus \mathrm{span}(B) \) and \( Y \) is a random vector such that \( Y_i \)'s are i.i.d. with \( Y_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2) \). Then for all \( \varepsilon_1 \geq 0 \) and \( \varepsilon_2 > 0 \), we have:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add that B has columns of norm 1 and define q:=(X+Y)/‖X+Y‖₂ (the normalized noisy column); the statement then has a determinate meaning matching the proof's use of cor:cond-ls and thm:noise-ls.
issues.overall_effect: cor:main cannot be evaluated as stated; cor:added-2, which applies it at each QR iteration with q=â_i, inherits the ill-posedness.
issues.title: cor:main: added column q undefined and missing unit-column hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local addition (one definition plus one standard hypothesis) that makes the statement well-defined without altering its form or guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows by recognizing that $\frac{1+\sqrt{1 -  \|r\|_2^2}}{ \|r\|_2}$ is a decreasing function of $\|r\|_2$, and then applying Corollary \ref{cor:cond-ls} and Theorem \ref{thm:noise-ls}.

issues.failure_explanation: On the event ‖r‖₂≥1/√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²) the decreasing bound g(s)=(1+√(1−s²))/s gives κ([B,q])≤κ(B)·g(1/√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²))=κ(B)(√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)+ε₁/ε₂)=κ(B)(√(ε₁²+ε₂²)+ε₁)/ε₂, not κ(B)ε₁√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²). The stated factor is smaller and the claim is false: for orthonormal B (κ(B)=1) and ε₁=ε₂=1, the event ‖r‖≥1/√2 has positive probability and at ‖r‖=1/√2 one has κ([B,q])=1+√2≈2.414>√2, contradicting the claimed bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor by √(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)+ε₁/ε₂ (equivalently (√(ε₁²+ε₂²)+ε₁)/ε₂); the corollary's form and cor:added-2's product structure survive with the corrected factor.
issues.overall_effect: The probabilistic bound in cor:main is false; cor:added-2's final product bound ∏(ε_{1,i}√(1+(ε_{1,i}/ε_{2,i})²)) inherits the wrong factor at every iteration.
issues.title: cor:main: incorrect condition-number factor (wrong evaluation of the decreasing function)
issues.why_classification: The stated bound is demonstrably false, but the correct factor is unambiguous and the corollary's guarantee (a probabilistic κ-bound of comparable form) survives, so the repair is contained though not a mere typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The event E_i bounds κ(âQ[:,i]) through κ(âQ[:,i−1]), so cor:main must be applied with B=âQ[:,1:i−1], which has i−1 columns; the noncentral F degrees of freedom should be F′_{m−i+1, i−1}, not F′_{m−i,i}. The proof's display further uses an undefined w_i (presumably a_i) and the probability display drops the indices on ε₁, ε₂ (should be ε_{1,i}, ε_{2,i}); together with the inherited unsquared argument (thm:noise-ls) and wrong factor (cor:main), the advertised probability and product bound are unreliable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the degrees of freedom to F′_{m−i+1, i−1} with the correspondingly indexed argument, replace the undefined w_i by a_i, and restore the indices on ε_{1,i}, ε_{2,i}; the union-bound and telescoping-product structure survives.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's final QR result: the per-iteration probability is computed with the wrong degrees of freedom and undefined symbols, so the stated probability guarantee (and hence the final product bound on κ(âQ)) is not established.
issues.title: cor:added-2: off-by-one F degrees of freedom and undefined symbols in the probability guarantee
issues.why_classification: The defects are index-level and require recomputing the probability expression, but the corollary's architecture (union bound over E_i, telescoping product) is preserved; a contained repair with no new global argument.
